title: A lower bound for the Schur numbers
statement:
For every integer $n \ge 3$, the Schur number $s_n$ satisfies
\[27\cdot 3^{\,n-3} + 1 \;\le\; 2\,s_n,\]
equivalently $s_n \ge \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(27\cdot 3^{\,n-3} + 1\bigr)$.
replaced:
\emph{Using (a) and the fact that \texttt{s$_{3}$ = 14}, show that
\texttt{s$_{n}$ $\ge$ $\tfrac{1}{2}$(27$\cdot$3\textasciicircum{}\{n-3\} + 1)}.}

(\emph{b}) Using (\emph{a}) and the fact that $s_3 = 14$, show that $s_n \geq
\frac{1}{2}(27(3)^{n-3} + 1)$. (A better lower bound has been obtained by Abbott and
Moser, 1966.)
